amorphous

uh-MOR-fus -- stress on the second syllable, MOR. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Amorphous is without defined shape or form.

The jellyfish drifted past like an amorphous ghost, its edges impossible to trace in the dark water.

Example

A lava lamp's glowing wax stays amorphous as it rises and falls, stretching, splitting, and merging, never holding a single outline for more than a second.

It has no defined shape or form, only an endless flow from one blob to the next. Amorphous works for ideas too -- an amorphous plan is one that has never taken clear shape.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

shapeless: Shapeless is the everyday word for one thing that lacks a definite outline -- a shapeless bag, a shapeless old coat. Amorphous is the more formal cousin and reaches abstractions too: an amorphous fear or organization. A sweater can be shapeless; a plan or a dread is amorphous.

unstructured: Unstructured means missing organized arrangement -- an unstructured essay or meeting has parts, just no plan holding them together. Amorphous is more radical: no clear shape at all, not even messy parts to rearrange. An unstructured day still has events; an amorphous day would be pure fog.

fluid: Fluid describes something that keeps changing -- a fluid situation shifts from hour to hour, a fluid lineup changes every game. Amorphous says a thing never had a clear shape at all. A fluid plan keeps changing; an amorphous plan was never definite to begin with.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

defined: having clear form, limits, or outline

structured: arranged in a clear, organized pattern

Where it sits · how completely shape is missing

nebulous → amorphous → formless

nebulous vs. amorphous: Nebulous is softer than amorphous -- a nebulous idea is merely hazy at its edges, while an amorphous one has no discernible shape anywhere at all.

formless vs. amorphous: Formless pushes even past amorphous: an amorphous cloud still has substance you can point to, while something formless lacks any form whatsoever, as if it could never hold a shape even for a moment.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — a-: without; not (Greek a- (the 'alpha privative'))

root — morph: form, shape (Greek morphe 'form')

suffix — -ous: full of; possessing the qualities of (Latin -osus, via Old French -ous)

Put it together: Amorphous uses the -ous variant of this unit's suffix family -- but watch the reversal! Greek a- ('without') sits in front of morph ('form'), so instead of the usual 'full of' reading, amorphous literally means 'possessing the quality of having no form.' The prefix flips the suffix's normal sense: this is the one word in the unit where -ous marks the fullness of an absence.

Use the root in a new word: metamorphosis: Biology class spent the whole week on the stages of metamorphosis.

Root Check

Word Choice

Amorphous covers both the physical and the abstract: an amorphous blob of dough, but also an amorphous fear, an amorphous organization, an amorphous plan. Whenever something -- object or idea -- refuses to take a clear shape, amorphous is the word.
